description: Computing with the three-dimensional structures of proteins and their ligands: levels of protein structure, structure databases and visualisation, structural comparison, secondary and tertiary structure prediction including deep learning methods, molecular docking and the computational stages of drug discovery. Practised with browser-based molecular viewers and docking simulations on public structures, with targets drawn from malaria, sickle cell disease and neglected tropical diseases.
modelledOn: Branden and Tooze, Introduction to Protein Structure
Leach, Molecular Modelling: Principles and Applications
Petsko and Ringe, Protein Structure and Function
outcomes: Describe primary, secondary, tertiary and quaternary protein structure and relate the physical forces that stabilise folds to structure and function.
Retrieve, validate and visualise experimental structures from the Protein Data Bank and judge their quality from resolution, R-factors and validation reports.
Superpose and compare structures with RMSD, TM-score and structural alignment algorithms and classify folds with CATH and SCOP.
Predict secondary and tertiary structure with statistical, homology-based and deep learning methods and assess the confidence of a prediction.
Prepare receptors and ligands, run molecular docking and interpret poses and scores with an understanding of their limitations.
Design a structure-based drug discovery workflow from target selection through virtual screening to ADMET filtering.

units.title: Protein structure levels
topics: Amino acids and the peptide bond; backbone torsion angles phi, psi and omega; the Ramachandran plot
Secondary structure: alpha helices, beta sheets, turns and loops; hydrogen-bonding patterns
Tertiary structure: motifs, domains and folds; the hydrophobic effect, salt bridges, disulphide bonds
Quaternary structure and assemblies; haemoglobin as a model of cooperativity and allostery
Protein folding and stability: Anfinsen's experiment, energy landscapes, Levinthal's paradox
How one substitution changes structure: HbS polymerisation in sickle cell disease

units.title: Experimental methods, databases and visualisation
topics: X-ray crystallography, NMR and cryo-electron microscopy: what each measures and its limits
The Protein Data Bank: PDB and mmCIF formats, chains, residues, atoms, B-factors, occupancy
Assessing structure quality: resolution, R and R-free, validation reports, Ramachandran outliers
Visualising and selecting structures in Mol* and PyMOL: cartoons, surfaces, electrostatics, binding sites
Related resources: UniProt, PDBsum, the AlphaFold Protein Structure Database

units.title: Structure comparison and classification
topics: Optimal superposition: the Kabsch algorithm and root-mean-square deviation
Structural alignment when sequences differ: DALI, CE and TM-align; TM-score and GDT
Fold classification with CATH and SCOP; convergent and divergent evolution of folds
Structure conservation beyond sequence similarity; detecting remote homologues
Contact maps, distance matrices and solvent accessibility

units.title: Secondary structure prediction
topics: Assigning secondary structure from coordinates with DSSP
Early statistical methods: Chou-Fasman and GOR propensities
Neural network predictors using evolutionary profiles (PSIPRED); accuracy measures Q3 and SOV
Predicting transmembrane helices, disordered regions and signal peptides

units.title: Protein structure prediction
topics: Homology modelling: template search, target-template alignment, model building, loop modelling (MODELLER, SWISS-MODEL)
Threading and fold recognition; fragment assembly and ab initio methods (Rosetta)
Coevolution and contact prediction from multiple sequence alignments
Deep learning prediction with AlphaFold and RoseTTAFold: architecture in outline, pLDDT and PAE confidence measures
Assessing models: the CASP experiments, MolProbity, knowing when a prediction should not be trusted
Modelling a Plasmodium falciparum protein with no experimental structure

units.title: Molecular mechanics and dynamics
topics: Force fields: bonded and non-bonded terms, partial charges, solvation models
Energy minimisation by steepest descent and conjugate gradients
Molecular dynamics: integrating Newton's equations, timesteps, thermostats, periodic boundaries
Analysing trajectories: RMSD and RMSF, flexibility and conformational change

units.title: Molecular docking
topics: Protein-ligand interactions: hydrogen bonds, hydrophobic contacts, pi stacking, binding affinity
Binding site detection and receptor preparation: protonation, waters, missing atoms
Ligand preparation: SMILES, 3D conformers, tautomers, charges; chemical databases such as PubChem and ChEMBL
Search algorithms and scoring functions in AutoDock Vina; rigid and flexible docking
Validating a docking protocol by redocking a crystal ligand; false positives and the limits of scores
Docking candidate inhibitors into Plasmodium falciparum dihydrofolate reductase

units.title: Drug discovery workflows
topics: The drug discovery pipeline: target identification, hit finding, lead optimisation, preclinical and clinical stages
Virtual screening: structure-based and ligand-based approaches, pharmacophores, similarity search
Drug-likeness and ADMET prediction: Lipinski's rule of five, toxicity filters
QSAR modelling and machine learning for activity prediction
Case studies: antimalarials such as artemisinin derivatives, open-source drug discovery for neglected tropical diseases, natural products from African medicinal plants

units.title: Project
topics: Choosing a disease target and gathering structural and chemical data
Building or retrieving a structure, preparing it and running a small virtual screen
Reporting results with figures, confidence assessment and limitations
Project: a structure-based screening report for a target relevant to health in Africa

schedule.title: Backbone geometry and protein folds
schedule.exercise: Short problem set: compute phi and psi from four atoms, classify five residues on a Ramachandran plot and name the hydrogen-bond pattern of a helix.

tasks.title: Compute the phi, psi and omega torsion angles of three residues from backbone coordinates and mark them on a Ramachandran plot
Classify the residues of a short PDB chain as helix, sheet or coil using hydrogen-bond patterns and torsion angles, and compare with the file annotation
Identify the hydrophobic core, salt bridges and disulphide bonds of a small protein from its coordinates and report the residue pairs

schedule.title: Quaternary structure and sickle cell disease
schedule.exercise: Write a half-page explanation of how the HbS mutation causes polymerisation, with a diagram of the contact it creates.

tasks.title: Compare the four chains of haemoglobin in a PDB file and measure the distances between subunits to describe the interfaces
Plot a simple energy landscape for a folding protein and use Levinthal's calculation to show why random search of conformations cannot work
Compare normal and sickle haemoglobin structures at position 6, measure the new hydrophobic contact and explain how it favours polymerisation

schedule.title: Experimental methods and structure databases
schedule.exercise: Compare X-ray, NMR and cryo-EM models of one protein, and write down what each reports about uncertainty.

tasks.title: Parse a PDB file to list its chains, residue counts, B-factors and occupancies, and print a summary of each chain
Assess the quality of three structures of one protein from resolution, R-free and Ramachandran outliers and rank which to trust
Select a binding site by residue and distance, compute its surface and electrostatic character and report which residues line it

schedule.title: Superposition and fold comparison
schedule.exercise: Superimpose two structures by hand on a small set of points and compute their RMSD.

tasks.title: Superimpose two sets of five points with the Kabsch algorithm and compute the RMSD before and after alignment
Compute a structural alignment of two proteins of different sequence, report RMSD, TM-score and aligned length and say if they share a fold
Classify five proteins into CATH-style classes and architectures from their structural similarity matrix and explain a possible convergent evolution case

schedule.title: Contact maps and remote homology
schedule.exercise: Draw the contact map for a small protein and mark the helices and strands it reveals.

tasks.title: Compute a distance matrix and a contact map at an 8 Angstrom threshold for a small protein and identify the helices as diagonal bands
Compute solvent accessibility for each residue, classify buried versus exposed, and compare to hydrophobicity along the sequence
Detect a remote homologue pair with low sequence identity but high structural similarity and report the evidence for the relationship

schedule.title: Secondary structure assignment and prediction
schedule.exercise: Apply Chou-Fasman rules by hand to a short sequence and compare with the DSSP assignment.

tasks.title: Assign secondary structure from coordinates using a simplified DSSP-style hydrogen-bond rule and compare with the file's annotation
Implement Chou-Fasman propensity prediction for a sequence and report Q3 against the true assignment
Predict transmembrane helices and signal peptides in five sequences with a hydropathy window and check the predictions against known annotations

schedule.title: Protein structure prediction
schedule.exercise: Write a short plan for modelling a protein with 40 percent identity to a known template, including checks on the model.

tasks.title: Align a target sequence to a template and build a homology model by copying the template backbone, noting which regions are loops
Predict residue contacts from coevolution by computing mutual information on a small alignment and compare with true contacts
Compare homology modelling, threading and fragment assembly on three targets of different template quality and recommend the best for each

schedule.title: Deep learning models and malaria targets
schedule.exercise: Short report on how much you trust each region of a predicted structure, with reasons from the confidence scores.

tasks.title: Read pLDDT and PAE values for a predicted structure and mark regions of low confidence on the sequence
Validate a predicted model with Ramachandran statistics and clash checks and decide which regions should not be trusted
Model a Plasmodium falciparum protein with no experimental structure, assess confidence regions and list what questions the model can and cannot answer

schedule.title: Force fields and molecular dynamics
schedule.exercise: Calculate a Lennard-Jones and Coulomb energy for two atoms by hand and explain why periodic boundaries are used.

tasks.title: Plot the Lennard-Jones potential for two atoms, find its minimum and add a Coulomb term for two partial charges
Minimise the energy of a small peptide with steepest descent and conjugate gradients and compare how fast each converges
Write a small molecular dynamics loop for 30 particles with velocity Verlet, a thermostat and periodic boundaries, and monitor total energy

schedule.title: Docking preparation
schedule.exercise: Prepare a receptor and a ligand for docking and write a checklist of the preparation steps with the reason for each.

tasks.title: Count hydrogen bonds and hydrophobic contacts between a bound ligand and protein in a PDB file and list the interacting residues
Prepare a receptor by removing waters, adding hydrogens and filling a missing side chain, then identify the pocket from the co-crystal ligand
Convert five SMILES strings into 3D conformers with sensible charges and tautomers, and check the ligand properties against a database record

schedule.title: Docking and validation
schedule.exercise: Write a validation plan for a docking protocol and the criteria that would make you distrust its scores.

tasks.title: Dock a ligand into a rigid receptor with a simple scoring function, score five poses and rank them by energy
Redock a crystal ligand, calculate pose RMSD to the experimental position and decide whether the protocol passes a 2 Angstrom threshold
Dock ten candidate inhibitors into the P. falciparum dihydrofolate reductase site, rank them, and discuss which scores you would not trust

schedule.title: Drug discovery workflows
schedule.exercise: Write a one-page plan for a virtual screen against a neglected tropical disease target, including filters and validation.

tasks.title: Place activities on the drug discovery pipeline from target selection to clinical trials, choosing the next step at each stage with evidence
Apply Lipinski's rule of five and a toxicity filter to 30 compounds and list the ones that pass each criterion
Build a QSAR model on an activity dataset, validate it with a hold-out set and report which structural features drive predicted activity

schedule.title: Screening project
schedule.exercise: Project report: a structure-based screen for a health target in Africa, with figures, confidence assessment and limitations.

tasks.title: Select a disease target, fetch its structure and ligand data and summarise the quality and coverage of the available evidence
Prepare a structure, run a small virtual screen of 50 compounds, and rank the hits with a pose-quality check
Produce a structure-based screening report for an African health target with a validated docking protocol, a hit table and limitations section
